historical_references.reference: Varishka was a small republican state in northern India, believed to be located in the Upper Doab region of the Ganges. It was a powerful state in the 4th century BCE, during the period of Magadha Empire. Varishka is mentioned in the Buddhist text, Cullavagga, as a source of horses for the Magadhan king Bimbisara. The state apparently had a powerful cavalry and contributed significantly to the military might of the Magadhan Empire.

Another mention of Varish is found in the Rigveda, one of the oldest texts in Sanskrit literature. The hymn 1.111 is dedicated to Indra, in which Varish is mentioned as a river system that the god Indra brought to life. It is referred to as a source of the Saraswati river, which was the primary river system in north India during the Rigvedic period. The hymn suggests that Varish was an important river system in the early Vedic civilization.
